ESV.2: “Keep listening to my words, and let this be your comfort.
ESV.3: Bear with me, and I will speak, and after I have spoken, mock on.
ESV.4: As for me, is my complaint against man? Why should I not be impatient?
ESV.5: Look at me and be appalled, and lay your hand over your mouth.
ESV.6: When I remember, I am dismayed, and shuddering seizes my flesh.
ESV.7: Why do the wicked live, reach old age, and grow mighty in power?
ESV.8: Their offspring are established in their presence, and their descendants before their eyes.
ESV.9: Their houses are safe from fear, and no rod of God is upon them.
ESV.10: Their bull breeds without fail; their cow calves and does not miscarry.
ESV.11: They send out their little boys like a flock, and their children dance.
ESV.12: They sing to the tambourine and the lyre and rejoice to the sound of the pipe.
ESV.13: They spend their days in prosperity, and in peace they go down to Sheol.
ESV.14: They say to God, ‘Depart from us! We do not desire the knowledge of your ways.
ESV.15: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? And what profit do we get if we pray to him?’
ESV.16: Behold, is not their prosperity in their hand? The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
ESV.17: “How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out? That their calamity comes upon them? That God  distributes pains in his anger?
ESV.18: That they are like straw before the wind, and like chaff that the storm carries away?
ESV.19: You say, ‘God stores up their iniquity for their children.’ Let him pay it out to them, that they may know it.
ESV.20: Let their own eyes see their destruction, and let them drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
ESV.21: For what do they care for their houses after them, when the number of their months is cut off?
ESV.22: Will any teach God knowledge, seeing that he judges those who are on high?
ESV.23: One dies in his full vigor, being wholly at ease and secure,
ESV.24: his pails  full of milk and the marrow of his bones moist.
ESV.25: Another dies in bitterness of soul, never having tasted of prosperity.
ESV.26: They lie down alike in the dust, and the worms cover them.
ESV.27: “Behold, I know your thoughts and your schemes to wrong me.
ESV.28: For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?’
ESV.29: Have you not asked those who travel the roads, and do you not accept their testimony
ESV.30: that the evil man is spared in the day of calamity, that he is rescued in the day of wrath?
ESV.31: Who declares his way to his face, and who repays him for what he has done?
ESV.32: When he is carried to the grave, watch is kept over his tomb.
ESV.33: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; all mankind follows after him, and those who go before him are innumerable.
ESV.34: How then will you comfort me with empty nothings? There is nothing left of your answers but falsehood.”

NLT.2:
“Listen closely to what I am saying.
That’s one consolation you can give me.
NLT.3:
Bear with me, and let me speak.
After I have spoken, you may resume mocking me.
NLT.4:
“My complaint is with God, not with people.
I have good reason to be so impatient.
NLT.5:
Look at me and be stunned.
Put your hand over your mouth in shock.
NLT.6:
When I think about what I am saying, I shudder.
My body trembles.
NLT.7:
“Why do the wicked prosper,
growing old and powerful?
NLT.8:
They live to see their children grow up and settle down,
and they enjoy their grandchildren.
NLT.9:
Their homes are safe from every fear,
and God does not punish them.
NLT.10:
Their bulls never fail to breed.
Their cows bear calves and never miscarry.
NLT.11:
They let their children frisk about like lambs.
Their little ones skip and dance.
NLT.12:
They sing with tambourine and harp.
They celebrate to the sound of the flute.
NLT.13:
They spend their days in prosperity,
then go down to the grave in peace.
NLT.14:
And yet they say to God, ‘Go away.
We want no part of you and your ways.
NLT.15:
Who is the Almighty, and why should we obey him?
What good will it do us to pray?’
NLT.16:
(They think their prosperity is of their own doing,
but I will have nothing to do with that kind of thinking.)
NLT.17:
“Yet the light of the wicked never seems to be extinguished.
Do they ever have trouble?
Does God distribute sorrows to them in anger?
NLT.18:
Are they driven before the wind like straw?
Are they carried away by the storm like chaff?
Not at all!
NLT.19:
“‘Well,’ you say, ‘at least God will punish their children!’
But I say he should punish the ones who sin,
so that they understand his judgment.
NLT.20:
Let them see their destruction with their own eyes.
Let them drink deeply of the anger of the Almighty.
NLT.21:
For they will not care what happens to their family
after they are dead.
NLT.22:
“But who can teach a lesson to God,
since he judges even the most powerful?
NLT.23:
One person dies in prosperity,
completely comfortable and secure,
NLT.24:
the picture of good health,
vigorous and fit.
NLT.25:
Another person dies in bitter poverty,
never having tasted the good life.
NLT.26:
But both are buried in the same dust,
both eaten by the same maggots.
NLT.27:
“Look, I know what you’re thinking.
I know the schemes you plot against me.
NLT.28:
You will tell me of rich and wicked people
whose houses have vanished because of their sins.
NLT.29:
But ask those who have been around,
and they will tell you the truth.
NLT.30:
Evil people are spared in times of calamity
and are allowed to escape disaster.
NLT.31:
No one criticizes them openly
or pays them back for what they have done.
NLT.32:
When they are carried to the grave,
an honor guard keeps watch at their tomb.
NLT.33:
A great funeral procession goes to the cemetery.
Many pay their respects as the body is laid to rest,
and the earth gives sweet repose.
NLT.34:
“How can your empty clichés comfort me?
All your explanations are lies!”

WEB.23: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.
WEB.24: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.
WEB.25: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.
WEB.26: They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.
WEB.27: “Behold, I know your thoughts, the devices with which you would wrong me.

AMP.4:
"As for me, is my complaint to man or about him?
And why should I not be impatient and my spirit troubled?
AMP.5:
"Look at me and be astonished and appalled;
And put your hand over your mouth.
AMP.6:
"Even when I remember, I am troubled and afraid;
Horror and trembling take hold of my flesh.
AMP.7:
"Why do the wicked still live,
Become old, and become mighty in power?
AMP.8:
"Their children and descendants are established with them in their sight,
And their offspring before their eyes.
AMP.9:
"Their houses are safe from fear;
And the rod of God is not on them.
AMP.10:
"His bull breeds and does not fail;
His cow calves and does not miscarry.
AMP.11:
"They send forth their little ones like a flock,
And their children skip about.
AMP.12:
"They lift up their voices and sing to the tambourine and the lyre
And rejoice to the sound of the flute.
AMP.13:
"They fully enjoy their days in prosperity,
And so go down to Sheol (the nether world, the place of the dead) in a [peaceful] moment.
AMP.14:
"Yet they say to God, 'Depart from us,
For we do not desire the knowledge of Your ways.
AMP.15:
'Who [and what] is the Almighty, that we should serve Him?
And what would we gain if we plead with Him?'
AMP.16:
"But notice, the prosperity of the wicked is not in their hand (in their power);
The counsel of the wicked [and the mystery of God's dealings with the ungodly] is far from my comprehension.
AMP.17:
"How often [then] is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out,
And that their disaster falls on them?
Does God distribute pain and destruction and sorrow [to them] in His anger?
AMP.18:
"Are they like straw before the wind,
And like chaff that the storm steals and carries away?
AMP.19:
"You say, 'God stores away [the punishment of] man's wickedness for his children.'
Let God repay him so that he may know and experience it.
AMP.20:
"Let his own eyes see his destruction,
And let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
AMP.21:
"For what pleasure does he have in his house and family after he is dead,
When the number of his months [of life] is cut off?
AMP.22:
"Can anyone teach God knowledge,
Seeing that He judges those on high?
AMP.23:
"One dies in his full strength,
Being wholly at ease and quiet and satisfied;
AMP.24:
His pails are full of milk [his sides are filled out with fat],
And the marrow of his bones is moist,
AMP.25:
Whereas another dies with a bitter soul,
Never even tasting pleasure or good fortune.
AMP.26:
"Together they lie down in the dust,
And the worms cover them.
AMP.27:
"Behold, I know your thoughts,
And the plots by which you would wrong me.
AMP.28:
"For you say, 'Where is the house of the noble man?
And where is the tent, the dwelling place of the wicked?'
AMP.29:
"Have you not asked those who travel this way,
And do you not recognize their witness?
AMP.30:
"That evil men are [now] reserved for the day of disaster and destruction,
They will be led away on the day of [God's] wrath?
AMP.31:
"But who will confront him with his actions and rebuke him face to face,
And who will repay him for what he has done?
AMP.32:
"When he is carried to his grave,
A guard will keep watch over his tomb.
AMP.33:
"The [dirt] clods of the valley are sweet to him [and gently cover him],
Moreover, all men will follow after him [to a grave],
While countless ones go before him.
AMP.34:
"How then can you vainly comfort me with empty words,
Since your answers remain untrue?"

MSG.2:
"Now listen to me carefully, please listen,
at least do me the favor of listening.
MSG.3:
Put up with me while I have my say—
then you can mock me later to your heart's content.
MSG.4:
"It's not you I'm complaining to—it's God.
Is it any wonder I'm getting fed up with his silence?
MSG.5:
Take a good look at me. Aren't you appalled by what's happened?
No! Don't say anything. I can do without your comments.
MSG.6:
When I look back, I go into shock,
my body is racked with spasms.
MSG.7:
Why do the wicked have it so good,
live to a ripe old age and get rich?
MSG.8:
They get to see their children succeed,
get to watch and enjoy their grandchildren.
MSG.9:
Their homes are peaceful and free from fear;
they never experience God's disciplining rod.
MSG.10:
Their bulls breed with great vigor
and their cows calve without fail.
MSG.11:
They send their children out to play
and watch them frolic like spring lambs.
MSG.12:
They make music with fiddles and flutes,
have good times singing and dancing.
MSG.13:
They have a long life on easy street,
and die painlessly in their sleep.
MSG.14:
They say to God, 'Get lost!
We've no interest in you or your ways.
MSG.15:
Why should we have dealings with God Almighty?
What's there in it for us?'
MSG.16:
But they're wrong, dead wrong—they're not gods.
It's beyond me how they can carry on like this!
MSG.17:
"Still, how often does it happen that the wicked fail,
or disaster strikes,
or they get their just deserts?
MSG.18:
How often are they blown away by bad luck?
Not very often.
MSG.19:
You might say, 'God is saving up the punishment for their children.'
I say, 'Give it to them right now so they'll know what
they've done!'
MSG.20:
They deserve to experience the effects of their evil,
feel the full force of God's wrath firsthand.
MSG.21:
What do they care what happens to their families
after they're safely tucked away in the grave?
MSG.22:
"But who are we to tell God how to run his affairs?
He's dealing with matters that are way over our heads.
MSG.23:
Some people die in the prime of life,
with everything going for them—
MSG.25:
Others die bitter and bereft,
never getting a taste of happiness.
MSG.26:
They're laid out side by side in the cemetery,
where the worms can't tell one from the other.
MSG.27:
"I'm not deceived. I know what you're up to,
the plans you're cooking up to bring me down.
MSG.28:
Naively you claim that the castles of tyrants fall to pieces,
that the achievements of the wicked collapse.
MSG.29:
Have you ever asked world travelers how they see it?
Have you not listened to their stories
MSG.30:
Of evil men and women who got off scot-free,
who never had to pay for their wickedness?
MSG.31:
Did anyone ever confront them with their crimes?
Did they ever have to face the music?
MSG.32:
Not likely—they're given fancy funerals
with all the trimmings,
MSG.33:
Gently lowered into expensive graves,
with everyone telling lies about how wonderful they were.
MSG.34:
"So how do you expect me to get any comfort from your nonsense?
Your so-called comfort is a tissue of lies."
